cards.text: We're in the temple courts, and Jesus is teaching. This time, HE'S the one asking the question. It's about the scribes, the teachers of the law, and what they say about the Christ, God's promised King.

cards.question: Jesus brings up what the scribes teach. What do the scribes say the Christ is?

cards.text: Then Jesus brings up David, Israel's king. Speaking by the Holy Spirit, David himself declared a line where the Lord speaks to someone David calls “my Lord.”

cards.question: In David's line, what does the Lord tell David's Lord to do until His enemies are under His feet?

cards.text: Here's what Jesus points out: David himself calls the Christ “Lord.” Friend, six little cookie cutters called me Papa for YEARS, and not ONE time did I turn around and call any of them “my lord.”

cards.question: If David himself calls the Christ “Lord,” what does Jesus ask?

answers.text: So how can He be David's son
So why did David write songs
So where will He be born

cards.question: There's a large crowd taking all this in. True or false: they listen to Jesus with delight.

cards.text: Jesus keeps teaching, and He says, “Watch out for the scribes.” They like to walk around in long robes and get greeted in the marketplaces, like that coworker who takes the LONG way to his desk so everybody HAS to say good morning.

cards.question: In the synagogues, the scribes want the chief seats. And at banquets, they want the places of ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus stops talking about the robes and the seats. Now He's talking about what these men DO.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says the scribes defraud orphans of their houses.
Jesus says the scribes defraud widows of their houses, and they make lengthy prayers for a ___.
What does Jesus say these scribes will receive?

cards.text: Jesus sits down opposite the treasury and watches the crowd putting money in. Many rich people put in large amounts, and me? The most money I've ever been near was my own 25-cent price sticker.

cards.question: Then one poor widow comes up to the treasury. What does she put in?

cards.text: All together, her coins are worth a small fraction of a denarius, like two chocolate chips left at the bottom of the bowl. Then Jesus calls His disciples over.

cards.question: Jesus tells His disciples, “Truly I tell you…” True or false: He says this poor widow has put in more than all the others.
How can the widow's two little coins be MORE than all those large amounts?

answers.text: She gave all she had to live on
She gave with a long loud prayer
She gave before anyone else did

cards.question: Jesus says the others all gave out of their ___, but she gave out of her ___.

findings.problem: The coworker comparison makes the scribes the butt of the joke. It mocks their attention-seeking through a made-up coworker. A joke that needs a target should land on Papa Dorin himself, and humor about people in the passage shouldn't laugh at them.

rule.text: When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself. Humor about people in Bible stories laughs with their human situation, never at them.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing from Mark 12:40. It only announces a turn in Jesus' teaching ("stops talking about the robes and the seats" and "what these men DO"), so no part of the passage moves forward on it. It should tell part of verse 40 as the setup for cards 11 to 13, for example that Jesus moves from what the scribes like to how they treat people.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card cites Mark 12:40, but it uses no content from that verse, so the citation doesn't match what the card tells.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
